newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tea prices rise on good auction demand.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tea prices rise on good auction demand.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea prices rose at the Colombo auction on good demand from the traditional Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and Middle East markets, brokers said on Wednesday. Among low grown teas, the mainstay of the auction, better OP1s and BOP1s were irregular while all other leafy grades and semi leaf varieties gained two to three rupees, they said. The CIS, Turkey, Dubai and Libya were active, they said.
High grown better Westerns fell three to five rupees while a few high priced teas of last week that did not maintain liquors lost a further five rupees per kg.

Prices of other Westerns and Uva/Udapussellas rose. Brokers Forbes and Walker said the anticipated average auction price for the 5.6 million kg on offer rose to 118.50 rupees ($2.03) from 117.14 last week. The next auction is on June 17-18 where six million kg will be on offer.
